notes:
Passed on the fake backend by python3 -m mhs.driver check (evidence contract_checked, never an MHS-Device level; no gate finding, warning or PDF citation). Model-authored and unreviewed: nothing here ran on an analyser; the hardware backend was never opened. The package is R1, so the loader does not refuse its hardware backend until reviewed_by is signed -- do not enable it without a person deciding to. This is a driver-pack card: the first entry symbol, anritsu_MS2830A.anritsu_MS2830A:Driver_VISA, is the implemented device; the other four entry symbols (yenista_CT400 Laser, agilent_N5277A Driver_VISA, anritsu_MS9740A Driver_VISA, srs_SR830 Driver_VISA) are separate devices in the same repository and are not covered. DEVIATION FROM THE CARD: the package uses a direct decorated Driver rather than the card's PythonObjectDriver helper, because Driver_VISA owns a Frequency sub-module and a pyvisa controller and a direct Driver expresses the scalar subset without a family table. The card's mock_strategy names the upstream dummy driver, but dummy/dummy.py implements a different device class (not Driver_VISA), so no upstream simulator of this analyser exists; the fake is the in-package in-memory stand-in. NOT COVERED: the trace arrays frequency(GHz) and power that the upstream get_waveform returns as a DataFrame from TRAC? TRAC1; this package carries the scalar marker powers and the sweep settings only. Every limit is operator_required because no text file of the clone states a range; site-limits.example.json is an example overlay, not a statement about a unit. gate.digest is the digest the check printed (the report without its clock); check-report.json is regenerated by every gate run and is not part of the package.
